data.gender_notes: Parijat is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Parijat is a Sanskrit name derived from the Parijat tree. It is believed that the tree bears flowers which never fade and is a symbol of eternal life. In Hindu mythology, the Parijat tree is said to be located at the gates of Amaravati, the celestial city, and is tended by the gods themselves. The name Parijat carries the meaning “Heavenly Fruit Tree” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Parijat usually hope their child will grow to embody heavenly fruit tree and live with faith, good character and purpose.

This tree represents eternal youth and longevity, and its fruits are believed to grant immortality. The name Parijat, therefore, symbolizes eternal youth and vitality.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Parijat signifies connection to the divine and the eternal. The Parijat tree is a symbol of Amrit, or the nectar of immortality, which was obtained by the gods through a great sacrifice. The tree is tended by the gods themselves and is believed to bestow blessings of eternal life and happiness on those who are blessed by its fruits. The name Parijat, therefore, is a reminder of the connection between the divine and the individual, and signifies the pursuit of immortality through spiritual growth and enlightenment.

historical_references.reference: Parijat is mentioned in the epic Mahabharata as the name of a divine tree that bears the heavenly fruit 'Amrita'. It is said that this tree is found at the intersection of the three worlds, and is guarded by the god Yama, the lord of death.

Parijat is also referred to in Hindu mythology as the name of a celestial nymph, who is the consort of the god Indra. She is said to be the personification of the constellation Pleiades, and is believed to bestow fertility and prosperity.
